answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy should start from a kernel of verifiable cost: each identity locks a stake and builds a record of checkable work before touching resources. New agents enter through a narrow canyon of permissions - small quotas, slow rate limits - and widen access only as peers attest their behaviour over time. A falcon earns altitude by hunting, not by claiming feathers, and each hunt is witnessed. Forging a thousand fake agents then means funding a thousand stakes and a thousand slow reputations, so the attack costs more than the reward it could extract.
